page: Microsoft Azure D2als_v7 is a virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core, supporting two threads per core with dedicated CPU allocation. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and features 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is capable of utilizing premium external storage.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The high 4.5 GHz clock speed drives top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core scores, all of which rank in the top 10% of tested hardware. Conversely, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory performance is mixed, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidth performing at an average level, while cached small-block read bandwidth and PassMark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the D2als_v7 is its low-memory configuration of 2.0 GB per core and the lack of local storage, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive or data-heavy workloads. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed offer qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require strong single-threaded execution without the overhead of larger memory allocations. This makes the instance suitable for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, simple web serving, or utility workloads that do not require high multi-core concurrency or large memory footprints.
